issue.title: bob gmail list -r fails the whole listing when one saved thread cannot be read

task_type_fields.impact: `bob gmail -r` is the only way to see which saved mail notes have fallen behind Gmail (notes refresh only on demand). One thread deleted in Gmail, or any single transient per-thread failure, hides drift for every other tracked thread. It also blocks scripting a "refresh stale notes" job on top of `list -r`. Fix size: per-row error handling in list.rs plus table/JSON rendering for a failed row, a fake-gog test, and the docs move.
task_type_fields.location: src/native/gmail/list.rs:103-113 (list::run, remote_message_count(...)? inside the per-row loop)
task_type_fields.repro:
Found by code reading during the Gmail thread ↔ note sync research (not yet reproduced live; apollo has no working gog read grant).

`list::run` with `--remote` loops over every displayed row and calls `search_peek::remote_message_count(...)?` (src/native/gmail/list.rs:103-113). The `?` propagates the first per-row error out of the whole command, so the listing prints nothing but one error document.

Repro (fake gog, the same way the Gmail tests do):
1. Save two threads in a temp vault, so `bob gmail list` shows two rows.
2. Point `BOB_GMAIL_GOG` at a fake gog whose `gmail thread get <id> --format metadata` returns a normal thread for one id and a 404 (the `gone` path) for the other.
3. Run `bob gmail list -a -r -f json`.

Expected: both rows are listed; the readable one has `new_messages`, the other is marked unreadable/gone (and the human table shows that row without a `+N new` count).
Actual: `{"ok": false, "error": {...}}`, with no rows at all.

Also fix while there: the `-r|--remote` paragraph in docs/gmail.md (line 574) sits under "## Link", not "## List".

issue.creation_reason: Found while researching how saved Gmail threads stay in sync with their mail notes: the only drift detector, `bob gmail list -r`, fails as a whole when any single thread cannot be read.

payload.description: Reply detection for linked tasks would likely build on list -r style remote counts; a per-row-tolerant remote count is a prerequisite-quality fix
bob gmail list -r reads saved threads through the same thread_metadata call
